hook.text: Barbara McClintock found genes that jump. In the 1940s, nobody believed her. She won the Nobel Prize in 1983.

buildup.text: Transposons—jumping genes—cut or copy themselves and land elsewhere in the genome. They're DNA parasites.

discovery.text: About 45% of the human genome is transposon-derived. Nearly half your DNA came from ancient jumping genes.

twist.text: Most are now inactive fossils. But some still jump, causing hemophilia, cancer, and other diseases when they land wrong.

climax.text: Transposons drove genome evolution. They shuffled genes, created new regulatory regions, and reshaped chromosomes.

punchline.text: Half your genome is made of ancient parasites.

quiz.question: What percentage of the human genome is transposon-derived?
